Subject: Initial question — voice notes / BAAs / retention

Hi Hannah,

Thanks for taking this. Quick context: Lifecare Health is evaluating vendors to ingest voice notes recorded by home health aides and short patient voice messages captured via our mobile app. We need clarity on: 1) whether Redwood will sign a BAA for audio-containing PHI, 2) what deployment options (hosted vs Dedicated vs Private) are required for PHI, and 3) recommended retention / transcription handling and any limitations for recording duration or redaction.

We also have a short procurement timeline — would be great to know whether a draft BAA and SOC 2 materials can be exchanged this week.

Hi Asha — thanks, and appreciate the spec. Short answers up front:

- Redwood will sign a BAA for workloads that process PHI when customers choose Dedicated or Private deployments.
- Hosted shared-tenant API currently cannot accept customer PHI under our standard hosted offering; there are narrow exceptions only under isolated, contractual arrangements (please see note below).
- Retention: we recommend configurable retention policies; typical customers set a 30–90 day rolling window for raw audio and keep transcripts for a separate retention policy. We support per-route retention TTLs on Dedicated/Private.

Longer explanation and next steps below. I'm looping in Monica (Security/Compliance) and Dev (Solutions) to provide the draft BAA and deployment notes.

Best,
Hannah Schmitt

Hi Asha — Monica here from Compliance. Thanks for outlining the use case. A few important operational points:

1) Deployment eligibility for PHI
   - Dedicated / Reserved Capacity: Approved for PHI. We run customer-dedicated GPU pools, separate tenant metadata, and can include customer-managed KMS.
   - Private (VPC / on-prem): Approved for PHI; suitable for highly regulated customers requiring network isolation and customer-managed infra.
   - Hosted shared tenancy: Not eligible for PHI under our standard terms. Exceptions require a legal review and are rare.

2) Ingestion and transcription options
   - We can accept raw audio over TLS and perform server-side transcription within the customer's Dedicated/Private environment.
   - Customers may choose to perform on-device or edge transcription prior to sending tokens if they want to avoid storing raw audio in Redwood.

3) Retention and redaction
   - We support configurable per-bucket and per-route TTLs. For audio we recommend a short TTL (30–90 days) and storing only transcripts when possible.
   - We provide automated redaction hooks (PII masking) at the tokenization/transcript level as a feature on Dedicated/Private.

4) Key management, logs, and audit
   - Customer-managed KMS (AWS KMS / GCP KMS / Azure Key Vault) supported on Dedicated/Private.
   - Audit logs (access, model calls, token counts) available and exportable for eDiscovery.

Attachments: I attached our standard BAA template and the most recent SOC2 Type II summary for your review.

Next practical steps: if you can sign the attached NDA/BAA draft, we can provision a Dedicated environment for a short proof-of-concept. If Lifecare prefers Private (VPC), we'll need a short infra questionnaire.

Regards,
Monica Patel
Compliance Manager, Redwood Inference

Hi Asha — Dev from Solutions here. Quick operational clarifications and a proposed minimal POC plan:

- Raw audio retention: In a Dedicated deployment, object storage for raw audio is configurable. By default our ingestion pipeline writes raw audio to a customer-scoped bucket for up to the configured TTL. We can implement an engine-only streaming mode for the POC where audio is streamed through the inference runtime and discarded immediately (no object persistence) — this requires a short feature flag and environment config.

- Transcript custody: We support two modes: (A) Redwood stores transcripts in customer-scoped storage (default in Dedicated) with customer-managed lifecycle; (B) transcripts can be POSTed to a customer-owned endpoint/S3 via an outbound connector immediately after generation, we can avoid persistent transcript storage in Redwood if you choose that flow.

- KMS / cost: KMS integration itself is supported and there is no separate per-token pricing for encryption. There may be a small one-time provisioning fee for key rotation policies and customer onboarding (~USD 2k), which we can roll into the POC budget.

Proposed POC (2 weeks):
1) Provision a Dedicated pool with customer-scoped storage and KMS.
2) Run a scripted ingest of 1,000 sample voice notes (you provide).
3) Switch to streaming-only ingestion on day 4 to validate no-persistence flow.
4) Deliver audit logs and transcript routing test.

If that sounds good, I can circulate a short SOW and DocuSign link.

Thanks,
Dev Patel
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
